newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two die as Typhoon Rosie threatens southwest Japan.
newsitem.headline: Two die as Typhoon Rosie threatens southwest Japan.

text.p: Typhoon Rosie moved closer to southwestern Japan on Saturday, killing two people and disrupting air, rail, road and ocean traffic.

Rosie, described by the agency as a "medium-sized but powerful" typhoon, was packing winds up to 144 kph (90 mph) and was expected to dump up to 80 cm (31 inches) of rain, the Meteorological Agency said.
At 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Saturday, the typhoon was about 50 km (31 miles) southeast of Japan's southwestern island of Shikoku, the agency said.
The storm, moving north at 20 kph (12.5 mph), has paralysed local air, land and ocean traffic.
A police spokesman in Yamaguchi prefecture in western Japan said that two people drowned while picking shellfish in a river.
Airport authorities said the typhoon forced the cancellations of more than 420 domestic flights, affecting some 53,000 travellers.
Bullet train services were also suspended in southwestern Japan and highways and expressways were closed.
The typhoon also forced the cancellations of most sports events scheduled for Sunday, including Japan's professional J.League soccer all-star match.
The typhoon was expected to cut through western regions of Japan's main island Honshu before moving over the Sea of Japan early on Sunday, the Meteorological Agency said.
